subject: science
passage: Before the 1930s, knowledge of India's birds rested largely on the notes of British officers and on specimens shipped to museums in Europe. The ornithologist Sálim Ali changed that by spending years in the field, often camping for months in remote districts to record which species lived where and in what numbers. Carrying out systematic surveys of several princely states, including Hyderabad and Travancore, on behalf of the Bombay Natural History Society, ______ The Book of Indian Birds, which he published in 1941 for ordinary readers, drew on those surveys and remains in print today.
stem: Which choice completes the text so that it conforms to the conventions of Standard English?

choices.A: Ali's reports built up a picture of the subcontinent's bird life region by region.
choices.B: a picture of the subcontinent's bird life was built up by Ali region by region.
choices.C: the subcontinent's bird life was mapped region by region in Ali's reports.
choices.D: Ali built up a picture of the subcontinent's bird life region by region.

explanation.why: The introductory phrase "Carrying out systematic surveys ..." describes the person doing the surveying, Ali. The subject right after the comma must therefore be "Ali," not his reports or the picture they produced.
explanation.A: Incorrect. The subject is "Ali's reports"; the reports did not carry out the surveys, Ali did.
explanation.B: Incorrect. The subject is "a picture," so the sentence says the picture carried out the surveys; the modifier dangles.
explanation.C: Incorrect. The subject is "the subcontinent's bird life," which did not carry out surveys.
explanation.D: Correct. "Ali" directly follows the modifier, so he is the one carrying out the surveys.
